description:
The boolean query filter lexer crashes the process when the query contains a non-ASCII character. Labels, assignees and values can be non-ASCII, so a batch update with such a filter aborts with a panic instead of running or reporting an error.

## Background

`jit issue update --filter <query>` parses its query with `Lexer` in `crates/jit/src/query_engine/lexer.rs`. The lexer keeps one cursor, `position`, but uses it under two units:

- `current_char` (lexer.rs:170-172) reads `self.input.chars().nth(self.position).unwrap()`, so the cursor counts characters.
- `is_at_end` (lexer.rs:178-180) compares the cursor with `self.input.len()`, which counts bytes.
- `read_word` (lexer.rs:146-163) slices `&self.input[start..self.position]` by bytes.

A multi-byte character makes the byte length exceed the character count. The lexer then reads past the last character and the `unwrap` panics, or it slices inside a character and the slice panics.

Reproduction in any initialised repository:

```
$ jit issue update --filter 'label:ä' --priority low
thread 'main' panicked at crates/jit/src/query_engine/lexer.rs:171:47:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
(exit 101)

$ jit issue update --filter 'label:ä state:ready' --priority low
thread 'main' panicked at crates/jit/src/query_engine/lexer.rs:161:22
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Tokenizing a filter that contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters, in field values or anywhere else, returns tokens or a parse error and never panics.
- [hard] REQ-02: A filter value with non-ASCII characters, such as `label:ä`, yields a filter token whose value is exactly the input text after the first colon.
- [hard] REQ-03: A filter combining non-ASCII terms with operators and parentheses, such as `label:ä AND (state:ready OR priority:high)`, yields the same token sequence as its ASCII equivalent with the values substituted.
- [hard] REQ-04: An invalid non-ASCII filter makes `jit issue update --filter` exit with an error status and an error message, not a panic exit.
- [hard] REQ-05: A regression test covers lexing of non-ASCII filter input, including a value ending in a multi-byte character and a multi-byte character followed by more terms. A property-based test asserts that the lexer never panics on arbitrary UTF-8 input.

## Notes

One fix is to make the cursor a byte offset and advance it by `ch.len_utf8()`. Another is to iterate with `char_indices`. Either way the cursor uses one unit throughout. `QueryParseError::UnexpectedChar` reports the cursor, so its position unit should be stated consistently.
title: Batch update filter panics on non-ASCII query text
